transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Alvarez (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (BrightHealth Head of ML), Ravi Singh (Infra), Hannah Lee (Product), Omar SRE, Sue Data

Summary (auto): quick sync to align on catalog pin choice and fallback test plan; agreed benchmarks and doc handoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is the weekly pilot sync, I think we're about 50 minutes out so plenty to cover, quick roll call?
[00:08] Janelle: hi Janelle here, yes
[00:10] Ravi: Ravi on infra, morning all
[00:12] Hannah: Hannah product
[00:15] Tom: tom here, se on the call, I'll own the bench runs with maya's help
[00:18] Omar: Omar SRE, will be monitoring traces for the window
[00:20] Maya: cool, goal today is to walk through the catalog matrix, confirm which model we pin in the pilot, and make sure our fallback orchestration is tested - also agree next steps for security docs.

[02:05] Janelle: quick context, our main concern is latency spikes during peak query patterns and occasional hallucinations on the clinical summarization prompts, we need a safe degrade that doesn't break throughput but keeps accuracy acceptable
[02:20] Maya: understood, that's the usual tradeoff; Tom, can you recap the three variants we suggested?
[02:26] Tom: sure - baseline is v1 (float16), second is v1-quant (int8-ish quant, leans cheaper but slightly more brittle on rare tokens), third is v1-small which is trimmed size for latency but loses some long-form coherence. In some labs v1-quant produced short hallucination glitches on long clinical lists, the kv cache sometimes mis-synced - noted as kv cash in older notes
[03:01] Ravi: when you say kv cash you mean KV cache, right? we saw odd token repeat in trace 2026-06-14
[03:07] Tom: yes kv cache, bad auto-correct in the auto transcript, yeah that one

[04:30] Hannah: how do we orchestrate fallback? are we thinking soft degrade (shorter max tokens) or hard swap to smaller variant?
[04:38] Maya: good question — two levers: runtime soft degrade (reduce max_new_tokens, increase sampling conservatism) or runtime hard swap which routes to v1-small. soft degrade keeps same model but tightens latency budget; hard swap is heavier but can guarantee latency under saturation if configured.
[05:05] Janelle: any empirical numbers on how much latency drops with v1-small?
[05:10] Tom: ballpark: tail p95 drops from ~420ms to ~210ms on our sample doc summarization bench at 1k prompt length. cost per token also drops ~30% on v1-small, quant variant reduces cost 40% but with occasional quality regression on specific medical token sets. I'll provide a spreadsheet.

[08:40] Ravi: and autoscale play? if we autoscale Dedicated vs Hosted, will fallback still work?
[08:48] Maya: yes — fallback routing is policy-driven; we can route by latency, cost, or region. If Dedicated pool is exhausted we can fallback to hosted variant with policy + rate limits. There's a short circuit for API keys and routing precedence.
[09:20] Omar: curious about KV cache warmup — when we switch models, warmup cost might spike, do we have warm-up strategies?
[09:28] Tom: yes we recommend prefix warmups and cache priming for heavy endpoints; Redwood has automatic prefix caching option but you'll need to choose TTLs. If we hard swap there's a cold-cache window; in most tests that's like 2-5 extra tokens latency for first requests.

[12:05] Hannah: security check — KMS options, audit logs, and data residency are deal breakers for us, where do you stand?
[12:15] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logs; we can deliver SOC2 artefacts and there's an on-prem option if your compliance team requires air-gap. We'll follow up with the SOC2 binder and KMS integration matrix.
[12:45] Janelle: perfect — need that for compliance review.

[14:10] Maya: ok let's run through a quick catalog matrix: row model / col dimension (latency, cost, fidelity, fallback behavior) - Tom, do you want to share screen? (screen share note)
[14:25] Tom: yes, pulling up the master sheet — v1: high fidelity, medium latency, medium cost, fallback: vertical degrade only; v1-quant: high-ish fidelity, low cost, some edge-case token errors; v1-small: lower fidelity, low latency, most predictable.
[15:05] Janelle: are there intermediate options like partial quant or per-layer quant?
[15:12] Tom: we do support mixed-precision and per-op kernel tuning, and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload. But per-layer quant needs evals on your prompt set.

[18:00] Ravi: about rollbacks — if we pin to v1 and see quality regressions after a rollout, what's the rollback runway?
[18:10] Maya: we have canary + instant rollback. Canary traffic can be set 1-10% for 24-72 hours, and you can set automatic rollback triggers on metric thresholds. Manual rollback is near-instant since routing reverts to the previous model hash. Note: if you change schema or tokenization between versions there are compatibility checks.
[19:00] Janelle: compatibility checks: will the platform warn if a KV cache format changes?
[19:05] Tom: yes it will flag incompatible caches and suggest soft purge or versioned cache lanes. There's a 'cache-compat' header.

[22:40] Hannah: can we test fallback under load? like a chaos test that kills a node and forces fallback to hosted?
[22:48] Maya: absolutely — we can simulate capacity exhaustion and trigger the soft/hard policies. We recommend a staged test: first bench then chaos test in staging.

[25:55] Janelle: ok on benchmarks, what inputs do you need from us?
[26:01] Tom: we need representative prompts — we asked for 10 families, ideally redacted clinical examples plus a few heavy tokenization edge cases. Also expected SLOs e.g., p95 < 500ms, cost target per 1k tokens, and acceptable accuracy drop threshold.
[26:20] Janelle: accuracy drop threshold — product wants under 3% QA degradation on key prompts.
[26:27] Maya: noted. We'll tag that as canary guardrail.

[30:00] Ravi: about metrics — what traces will you share vs what we host?
[30:08] Tom: we'll share aggregated latencies, token counts, and per-route cost breakdown. You keep raw traces; if you enable cross-account trace sharing we can ingest sample traces for correlation. We asked for a 24h trace window to start.

[33:10] Omar: slight crosstalk — when we route to hosted fallback, are we comfortable with PHI leaving the VPC?
[33:18] Maya: good point — routing to hosted may not be allowed for PHI. For PHI you should use Redwood Private or on-prem; otherwise we can anonymize and route. This is policy-level decision.

[36:40] Hannah: pricing again — if we use Dedicated with burst to hosted, how does billing split?
[36:48] Maya: billing is token-based across pools. Burst to hosted will bill hosted rates for those tokens; Dedicated commit discounts apply to Dedicated usage only. AE to send pricing sheet.

[40:05] Janelle: one more question on evals — can Redwood Optimize automatically recommend which model to pin based on our prompt families?
[40:15] Tom: yes, Optimize will run evals and recommend a quant/profile and pin. It can also suggest rollouts with guardrails. We'll produce a preliminary recommendation after you send prompts.

[44:30] Maya: recap then next steps: Redwood runs bench matrix (v1, v1-quant, v1-small) and shares spreadsheet; BrightHealth shares prompts + SLOs; security SOC2/KMS docs to be shared; schedule security deep dive next week.
[44:50] Janelle: sounds good.
[45:00] Hannah: can we get the fallback playbook doc?
[45:03] Maya: yes I'll send it tonight; it'll include rollback checklist and canary config examples.

[47:20] Ravi: one small ask — when you run benches please include warm and cold cache runs so we can see delta
[47:26] Tom: good call, we'll include warm/cold runs and sample traces

[49:40] Maya: any other blockers?
[49:45] Sue: none from data side
[49:48] Janelle: none, thanks team

[50:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.
